name: Mountain Pose (Tadasana)
description: The foundation of all standing poses. Improves posture, balance and body awareness — perfect for starting your day.
instructions: Stand tall with feet together or hip-width apart
Distribute weight evenly across both feet
Lengthen your spine and lift your chest
Relax shoulders away from ears
Arms alongside body, palms facing forward
Hold for 5–10 deep breaths

name: Warrior II (Virabhadrasana II)
description: A standing pose that builds strength and stability in the legs and core.
instructions: Step feet wide apart, front foot pointing forward
Bend front knee to 90 degrees over ankle
Extend arms parallel to the floor, palms down
Keep back leg straight and strong
Gaze over your front fingertips

name: Tree Pose (Vrikshasana)
description: A balancing pose that improves focus, stability and concentration.
instructions: Stand on one leg, finding your balance
Place foot on inner thigh or calf (never on knee)
Bring hands to prayer position at chest
Fix gaze on a steady point ahead
Hold 30 seconds then switch sides

name: Downward Dog (Adho Mukha Svanasana)
description: An inverted V-shape pose that stretches the whole body and relieves back pain.
instructions: Start on hands and knees in table-top position
Tuck toes and lift hips up and back
Straighten legs without locking knees
Press palms firmly into the mat
Let head hang between arms, ears level with upper arms

name: Chair Pose (Utkatasana)
description: A strengthening pose for legs, core and back — like sitting in an invisible chair.
instructions: Stand with feet hip-width apart
Bend knees and lower hips as if sitting in a chair
Keep weight in heels, knees above toes
Raise arms overhead, biceps by ears
Hold for 5 deep breaths

name: Triangle Pose (Trikonasana)
description: A side stretch that opens the hips and hamstrings. Great for spine flexibility.
instructions: Step feet wide apart, front foot pointing forward
Reach forward with front arm then lower to shin or floor
Extend top arm toward ceiling
Keep both legs straight and strong
Look up at top hand

name: Child's Pose (Balasana)
description: A restorative resting pose that gently stretches the back, hips and thighs. Perfect to do between poses.
instructions: Kneel on the floor, touch big toes together
Sit back on your heels and separate knees hip-width
Fold forward, extending arms in front or alongside body
Rest forehead on the mat
Breathe deeply and hold for 1–3 minutes

name: Cobra Pose (Bhujangasana)
description: A gentle backbend that strengthens the spine and opens the chest. Great for desk workers with back pain.
instructions: Lie face down, hands under shoulders
Press tops of feet and thighs into the mat
Inhale and lift chest off the floor
Keep elbows slightly bent, shoulders away from ears
Hold for 15–30 seconds then lower down slowly

name: Bridge Pose (Setu Bandhasana)
description: A gentle backbend lying on your back — strengthens the back and glutes, great for relieving lower back pain.
instructions: Lie on your back, knees bent, feet flat on floor
Place arms alongside body, palms down
Inhale and lift hips toward the ceiling
Press feet and arms firmly into the floor
Hold 5 breaths, then lower slowly

name: Seated Forward Bend (Paschimottanasana)
description: A calming pose that stretches the entire back body. Reduces stress and fatigue.
instructions: Sit on the floor with legs extended straight
Inhale and lengthen your spine tall
Exhale and hinge forward from hips (not waist)
Reach for feet, shins or ankles
Keep back long, avoid rounding excessively
Hold for 1–3 minutes

name: Standing Forward Bend (Uttanasana)
description: Releases tension in the spine and hamstrings. A great reset pose for the whole back.
instructions: Stand with feet hip-width apart
Inhale to lengthen the spine
Exhale and fold forward from the hips (not the waist)
Let head and neck hang heavy
Bend knees slightly if hamstrings are tight
Hold 30 seconds to 1 minute

name: Cat-Cow Stretch (Marjaryasana)
description: A gentle flowing movement that warms up the spine. Excellent for morning back stiffness.
instructions: Start on hands and knees in table-top position
Wrists under shoulders, knees under hips
Cow: Inhale, drop belly, lift chest and tailbone
Cat: Exhale, round spine to ceiling, tuck chin
Flow between the two with breath, 5–10 cycles

name: Legs Up the Wall (Viparita Karani)
description: A deeply restorative pose that relieves tired legs, reduces swelling and calms the nervous system.
instructions: Sit sideways next to a wall
Swing legs up the wall as you lie back
Scoot hips as close to wall as comfortable
Let arms rest at your sides, palms up
Close eyes and hold for 5–15 minutes
Great before bed or after long day of standing
